video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - Pick 8 In A 9 Cat H2H Draft

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team, 9-category head-to-head mock draft on Fantrax, picking 8th. He takes Anthony Edwards in round 1 and Austin Reaves in round 2. He follows with Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Onyeka Okongwu, Franz Wagner, Damian Lillard, Isaiah Hartenstein, CJ McCollum, Jusuf Nurkic, Paul Reed, Reed Sheppard, Isaiah... Jarace? no: Oso Ighodaro and Jaylin? MZ Johnson as late flyers. In almost every round from round 3 on, the player he wanted went one pick before his turn. That pushed his team toward blocks, weak assists and late fliers. Along the way he flags picks he sees as reaches (Jalen Johnson at 9, Stephon Castle, Darryn Peterson, Anthony Black, AJ Mitchell) and values (Tyrese Haliburton, Tyler Herro, Brandon Ingram, Michael Porter Jr.). He also reacts to a report that Jeremiah Fears and Yves Missi may start in New Orleans. His team finished first in the projected standings.

rules.text: When punting free throws around Giannis, you still need to get assists or threes in the early rounds. You do not need to chase low free throw guys.
rules.quote: You got to get you got to get assists or threes in these earlier rounds.

rules.text: Do not worry about a team tanking when drafting a good player from that team.
rules.quote: I'm not concerned with tanking and you shouldn't be either.

rules.text: Pairing two injury-risk stars (like Anthony Davis and Kawhi Leonard) on one team is very risky.
rules.quote: We can talk about value but pairing Anthony Davis and Kawhi Leonard is very risky.

rules.text: When your team is weak in a category like assists, do not overindex on chasing it.
rules.quote: So, I'm not going to overindex on chasing assists.

rules.text: Drafts vary a lot because many players have similar value. Stay adaptable instead of planning a perfect build.
rules.quote: There's so much variance with the similarities between players and overall value that you it's hard

rules.text: In 9-cat, do not draft players whose value comes mostly from points too early. This is not a points league.
rules.quote: Well, that is incredibly early on Steph Castle. This is not a points league, guys.

rules.text: Players coming back from Achilles injuries carry a risk of compensation injuries elsewhere in the body.
rules.quote: I'm just I'm a little cautious of compensation injuries, like a hamstring that caused him to miss a week and a half

rules.text: Avoid big reaches. A swing is fine, but a pick the player has almost no chance to beat is a mistake.
rules.quote: That's when I talk about don't make mistakes. Don't take trips on treacherous roads

rules.text: When you take a risky player, check how many other big risks are already on your roster. Do not stack risks.
rules.quote: Now, whenever you're taking a risky sort of option like Edy, is there any other big risks there?

rules.text: Drafting a backup center and waiting for the starter to be traded is usually a waste, especially if he is not a strong per-minute producer.
rules.quote: That's like a backup center that you're waiting for Sabonis to be traded. It may never happen

rules.text: Do not draft safe, low-upside veterans just to win the projected standings in the draft room.
rules.quote: sometimes they feel like they're used by people to try and win the projected standings in a draft

rules.text: In late rounds, ask whether a player is a starter or could become one.
rules.quote: Are they starters or can they be starters?

rules.text: Late-round fliers are often drops. You take them to see what their role turns out to be.
rules.quote: probably going to be drops, honestly. But we just want to see what their role turns out to be.

rules.text: Players who only pay off if someone else gets hurt are poor late picks.
rules.quote: Colin Gillespie, you're waiting on injuries for that to pay off cuz without injuries it won't.
